subject: Geofencing availability attestation and evidence requested
messages:
From: Anna Müller <anna.mueller@eurosys.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: compliance@eurosys.com
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request for geofencing availability attestation and supporting evidence

David,

Thanks for taking our call last week. As part of EuroSys' procurement and compliance review for the RFP (RFP-ES-2026-09) we need a short attestation and supporting artifacts about Redwood's geofencing / regional availability controls so we can validate no regulated data will leave the EU for our initial deployment. Please provide the following by end of month if possible: 

1) A signed attestation stating whether Redwood can guarantee EU-only processing for: a) request ingress, b) model execution, c) telemetry/analytics. 
2) Evidence/artifacts: configuration matrix that maps product modes (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) to deployment locality and data flow, a redacted SOC2 report, and a data flow diagram showing where logs/telemetry are generated and where they are stored.
3) Clarify fallback behavior: if the EU region is capacity constrained, will requests route to non-EU regions by default, or is there a customer-configurable opt-in?
4) Explain caching: are any ephemeral caches (prefix/KV) or CDN edge caches able to spill data to non-EU locations?
5) Key management: do you offer KMS/HSM integrations where keys remain in EU boundaries?
6) A statement on telemetry and analytics (what leaves the region, retention periods, pseudonymization).
7) A copy or pointer to any export-control or cross-border egress exceptions that might apply.

We will share these artifacts with our legal and infosec teams. If helpful, a short 30-45 minute technical walkthrough is welcome.

Best,
Anna

Subject: Re: Request for geofencing availability attestation and supporting evidence

Anna – thanks for the clear list. Attached are the artifacts we've prepared (see attachments list below) and short answers to each item so your team can triage quickly. Happy to schedule the walkthrough; Ben (sales engineering) and Laura (legal ops) are looped for any contract or SLA follow-ups.

Quick answers (high level):
1) Attestation: We can provide an attestation for EU-only processing for customer data when the account is provisioned in the EU region and the customer selects EU residency for Hosted or uses Redwood Dedicated / Private deployments located in EU data centers. The attached PDF (data-residency-attestation-ES.pdf) includes formal language and signature block.

2) Artifacts: Attached: regional-hosting-matrix.csv (maps Hosted/Dedicated/Private to region availability), data-flow-diagram.svg (visual), and a redacted SOC2 (soc2-report-redacted.pdf). We also included a short note on model variants: certain open-source model variants may require additional configuration to guarantee EU-only model runtime; we call this out in the matrix.

3) Fallback behavior: By default, Hosted accounts are routed to the nearest healthy region based on latency/cost policies. For customers requiring strict EU residency, we provide a per-account routing lock that prevents cross-region failover for the Hosted plan; Dedicated and Private are always provisioned in the chosen geography. The routing lock requires a config flag and is visible in the Console.

4) Caching: Automatic prefix/KV caching is enabled by default in Hosted to improve latency. For EU residency accounts with routing lock enabled, caches are pinned to EU nodes only. CDN edge caches used for static assets are configurable and can be set to EU-only. We document cache placement in the matrix and in the data flow diagram.

5) Key management: We support customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, and on-prem HSM options) with keys stored in customer-selected regions. For EU residency, keys can be provisioned and kept in EU key stores; our Private deployment supports FIPS/HSM connectors on-prem.

6) Telemetry & analytics: Operational telemetry (latency metrics, token counts) is collected for service health. For EU-residency accounts, telemetry aggregation and analytics processing occurs in the EU; raw request artifacts are redacted and retained according to the retention schedule in the attestation. Personally identifiable fields are pseudonymized before any cross-region movement. Retention defaults are 90 days for detailed logs and 13 months for aggregated metrics; both are configurable for Dedicated/Private.

7) Export controls / egress: We maintain a short export-control statement and a list of jurisdictional exceptions. Any statutory hold will be surfaced in the attestation.

Attachments included: data-residency-attestation-ES.pdf, regional-hosting-matrix.csv, soc2-report-redacted.pdf, data-flow-diagram.svg

Next steps: I can share a short walkthrough with our infra lead for the EU footprint next Tue/Wed. Please confirm availability; if your legal team wants any language edits we can route through Laura.

Regards,

Anna — quick clarifications below to help your privacy and infra teams: 

- CDN / edge cache controls: For Hosted customers, CDN/edge cache configuration is exposed in the Console for standard controls (cache TTL, region preferences). Changing cache placement to EU-only is available as a self-serve toggle for accounts with EU residency enabled; for older accounts or non-standard configurations our Ops team can apply the setting. Dedicated/Private deployments are configured at provisioning time and cache placement is a deployment parameter.

- Request-level metadata: For accounts provisioned with EU residency + routing lock, raw request-level metadata (source IP, timestamp, model variant) is processed and retained in EU-only processing pipelines. We do collect ephemeral transit logs to debug routing during incidents; those logs are redacted and pushed to EU storage for EU accounts. No raw request payloads or un-redacted metadata are forwarded to non-EU processors unless explicitly requested by the customer or compelled by lawful process.

- Latency SLO: We publish a latency target for the Dedicated product (p99 token latency under committed throughput) in the SLA. For Hosted customers, we publish empirical latency profiles per model and region in the Console and in the model catalog; we can offer a custom latency SLO for Hosted accounts by contract. Laura can follow up with suggested SLA language and options if you need a contractual SLO.
